title: Nested and array queries
summary: Query inside embedded objects and arrays using dot notation, $size and $elemMatch.

quiz.q: Which filter finds students whose address has city 'Salem'?
options: { address: { city: 'Salem' } } when the address also has a pin
quiz.explain: Dot notation needs quotes: `'address.city'`. The last option asks for an address exactly equal to `{ city: 'Salem' }`, and it would miss documents that also hold a pin.

quiz.q: Complete the operator to find students that have exactly three subjects.
quiz.explain: `$size` matches an array with exactly that many elements. It does not accept ranges like "at least 3".

quiz.q: A student has `subjects: ['maths', 'physics']`. How many students does this query match if that is the only student? Type the number.
quiz.explain: A plain value against an array field matches when any element equals it, so this student matches.

quiz.q: Why would you use `$elemMatch` instead of two separate conditions on `scores.subject` and `scores.mark`?
options: It forces one array element to satisfy all conditions together
It lets you query several arrays at once
It is the only way to read nested fields
quiz.explain: Without `$elemMatch`, different elements may satisfy different conditions, which gives false matches.

exercise.task:
Find the students who:

- live in **Madurai** (the city is inside `address`), and
- have a score entry for **maths** with a `mark` of **80 or more**. A single entry in `scores` must satisfy both.

Use dot notation for the city and `$elemMatch` for the score.
hints: You need two conditions in one filter: one on the nested city, one on the `scores` array.
Use `'address.city': 'Madurai'`. For `scores`, use `{ $elemMatch: { ... } }` with both subject and mark inside.
